en.title: Escape the Haunted Castle (Part 2)
en.description:
You are given a grid of passable cells and walls, along with a start, an exit, and some treasures. Each treasure can be picked up at most once. Find the minimum number of moves from the start to the exit; among all shortest paths, also find the maximum number of treasures that can be collected. If the exit cannot be reached, output `-1 0`.

OAMaster's Sentry #2 gives only the function's goal and one example, with no standard input format or bounds for online judging. The stdin/stdout protocol and constraints below are on-site definitions added by CSWork for this problem and do not represent the original OAMaster text.
en.input: The first line contains rows cols; the second line contains the number of walls wallCount; each of the next wallCount lines contains a wall coordinate row col; then the number of treasures treasureCount is given; each of the next treasureCount lines contains a treasure coordinate row col; the last two lines give the start and exit coordinates respectively. All coordinates are 0-based. On-site constraints: 1 <= rows, cols <= 200; all coordinates lie inside the grid; the start and exit are not walls; treasure coordinates are distinct. Duplicate wall coordinates are treated as the same wall.
en.output: Output two integers: the minimum number of steps and the maximum number of treasures that can be collected over all shortest paths. A treasure on the start cell counts toward the result; if the exit is unreachable, output `-1 0`.
en.explanation: First run BFS from start to get the shortest distance to every cell; then do DP in increasing order of distance, transitioning only from neighbors whose distance is 1 smaller, and record for each cell the maximum number of treasures over shortest paths that reach it.
